blocks.hero_subtitle: The A6 Avant is one of those wagons that makes sense if you want executive-car refinement with proper luggage space. On a 2025 import, the important part is getting the exact model code, drivetrain and listed equipment confirmed before bidding.
proof_points: Japan specialists with direct auction access
Importing estimate provided before bidding, with compliance as part of the process
blocks.why_kiwis_buy: People look at the A6 Avant because it gives them wagon practicality without stepping into an SUV. The body shape works well for luggage, golf clubs or airport runs, and quattro versions are worth a look if you want extra confidence on wet roads. One useful detail with this generation is that both front-wheel-drive and quattro examples have existed, so drivetrain needs to be confirmed on the exact car rather than assumed from the badge.
blocks.video_caption: From the front three-quarter angle you can see why the A6 Avant appeals to wagon buyers, long roofline, low load area and a shape that still looks like an executive Audi rather than a raised crossover. If the listing photos show the exact wheel design and tailgate setup, we can confirm those details before you bid.
blocks.main_usp_deep: What makes the A6 Avant interesting is the mix of executive-car manners and wagon usefulness. Mild-hybrid versions can add smoother stop-start behaviour in traffic, but the exact 2025 powertrain still needs to be confirmed on the individual vehicle. quattro is another drawcard on the right example, because it can give the A6 Avant the planted feel many buyers want for open-road work. This is not a budget wagon, it suits someone who wants refinement, space and the right specification rather than the lowest running costs.

buyer_persona.headline: Who is this car right for?
buyer_persona.body: This suits a buyer who wants a European wagon with a quieter, more composed feel than most mainstream options, and who still needs real luggage space. It also makes sense for someone who knows exact specification matters and wants the auction car checked properly before committing, so the car that arrives matches expectations as closely as the available information allows. If that sounds like you, it is a solid match.

car_specs_benefits.benefit: You get a lower load floor and more usable luggage space than a sedan, which matters more in daily use than a big boot number on paper.

car_specs_benefits.spec: Hybrid-assisted powertrain versions exist in this shape
car_specs_benefits.benefit: The electrical assistance can help smooth stop-start driving and reduce the busy feel you can get from a pure turbo setup in traffic.
On the right car, that gives better traction in heavy rain and a more settled feel on open-road trips.
It carries luggage and family gear without moving into a taller SUV driving position, which some buyers still prefer.

car_specs_benefits.benefit: That matters because driver-assist features, audio and drivetrain can change the ownership experience and the budget.

standout_features_block.headline: Features that stand out
standout_features_block.intro: On this model, the worthwhile features are the ones that change how it drives or how easy it is to live with.

items.title: quattro all-wheel drive
items.body: quattro is one of the main reasons buyers look at an A6 Avant rather than a standard front-wheel-drive wagon. On the right example it adds extra traction and a more planted feel in poor weather, which suits NZ motorway and open-road use. The exact drivetrain still needs to be confirmed on the auction car.
items.image_hint: Audi A6 Avant driving on a wet motorway with front three-quarter angle showing stable stance

items.title: Mild-hybrid assistance
items.body: Some versions in this shape use a mild-hybrid setup rather than a plug-in system. It adds electrical support around stop-start driving and low-speed transitions, which can make the car feel more polished in traffic. The exact 2025 setup still needs to be confirmed on the individual car.
items.image_hint: Instrument display showing energy flow or stop-start status while the car is stationary in city traffic

items.title: Avant luggage layout
items.body: The A6 Avant's shape is the practical bit people buy with their head. A long roof and wide tailgate opening make it easier to load bulky bags, pushchairs or travel cases than a sedan with a narrow boot opening. That is the real advantage of this body style.
items.image_hint: Rear tailgate open with suitcases loaded into the boot area

items.title: Driver-assist equipment worth confirming
items.body: On a 2025 car, the assist package can make a big difference to daily use, especially if you spend time on the motorway. Adaptive cruise, lane support and camera systems are the sort of items worth checking on the exact listing rather than assuming from the model name alone.
items.image_hint: Dashboard and steering wheel view with driver-assist graphics visible on the instrument display

tech_deep_dive_block.headline: What is actually fitted
tech_deep_dive_block.intro: With this model, the technical detail matters because specification can change a lot between auction cars.

items.title: Mild-hybrid system
items.body: This is not a plug-in setup. A mild-hybrid system uses a small electrical system to support the petrol powertrain during stop-start driving and some low-load moments, rather than driving long distances on battery power alone. In practice, the benefit is smoother restarts and a calmer feel in traffic. For a 2025 A6 Avant, the exact version needs to be confirmed on the individual car before any claim about output or economy is made.

items.title: quattro
items.body: quattro is Audi's all-wheel-drive system, and it is one of the main specification points buyers ask about on an A6 Avant. The reason is simple, it changes the car's character from a front-driven executive wagon to something that feels more secure when the road is wet or the weather turns. Not every example carries the same drivetrain, so this is one of the first things we confirm from the listing and model code.

items.title: Trim and equipment variation
items.body: This is where buyers can get caught out if they shop by photos alone. Audio, camera systems, wheel size, suspension setup and driver-assist equipment can all vary by trim and option pack. We use the auction information available for the exact vehicle to confirm what is listed, then separate confirmed equipment from model-level information so you know what is known before bidding.

faq_block.q: Can you confirm the exact specification of a 2025 A6 Avant before I bid?
faq_block.a: Yes. We review the auction information available for the exact vehicle and confirm the model code, listed drivetrain, mileage, grade, condition notes and any equipment clearly shown or stated.

faq_block.q: What costs make up the landed price?
faq_block.a: The main components are Vehicle cost, Japan-side costs, Shipping costs, AWA fee, Compliance, On-road costs and Customs clearance. We put those into an indicative landed-cost calculation for the exact car before you approve a bid.

faq_block.q: Can you tell me if it is typically within the entry requirements?
faq_block.a: Import viability must be checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding, and final certification occurs in NZ. We support you through that process, but the final outcome depends on the exact vehicle after arrival.

faq_block.q: How long does the process take?
faq_block.a: Timing depends on when the right car appears, the shipping schedule and the NZ arrival process. Once you are looking at live auction options, we can give you a clearer timeline based on the car and the sailing window.

faq_block.q: How do auction grades and condition notes help?
faq_block.a: The auction sheet gives useful information such as grade, mileage, damage markings and written notes from the auction house. We translate and explain those details so you know what is recorded. We also tell you what the available information does not prove.

blocks.company_positioning: ImportYourCar.co.nz is an NZ-based vehicle import service operated by Ultimate Motors Ltd. We have been helping buyers source cars from Japanese auctions since 2009, with support covering auction access, bidding, shipping coordination and the NZ arrival process.

not_for_you_block.headline: Who this may not suit
items: If your main priority is the lowest running-cost wagon possible, this is probably not the right place to start.
If you want a raised seating position or extra ground clearance, a wagon like the A6 Avant may feel too low compared with an SUV or crossover.
If you are not flexible on exact trim, drivetrain or equipment, be prepared to wait for the right auction car rather than forcing the first available one.

alternatives_block.intro: If you like the A6 Avant but want to compare it with other wagons sold in Japan or NZ, these are the main alternatives to weigh up.

rows.better_if: You want another European executive wagon with a slightly more driver-focused feel.
rows.tradeoff: Exact 2025 specification still needs to be confirmed per car, just as it does on the Audi.

rows.better_if: You prefer a softer, more comfort-led prestige wagon with a different cabin layout.
rows.tradeoff: Availability and exact trim mix vary by year and market, so the search can be narrower.

rows.better_if: You want wagon practicality with more ride height and a more relaxed NZ-road brief.
rows.tradeoff: It does not give you the same executive-car feel or low-slung road manners as the A6 Avant.
